titleTr: Yangın tatbikatı: genel kurallar ve unless

explainTr: Her zaman doğru olan şeyleri ve genel kuralları anlatırken zero conditional kullanırsın: If + present simple, present simple. If you heat ice, it melts. 'If' burada 'her seferinde' gibi çalışır, 'will' yoktur.
Güvenlik talimatlarında sonuç kısmı genelde talimat olur: If you hear the alarm, leave the room. Yani sonuç cümlesi yalın fiille başlayabilir.
'Unless' = 'if ... not' demektir (-medikçe). You can't enter unless you have a badge. Unless'ten sonra olumlu fiil gelir; 'unless you don't' yanlıştır, çünkü anlam zaten olumsuz.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'alarm çalarsa çıkarız' ve 'izin vermedikçe çıkamazsın' için -sa ve -medikçe ekleri vardır. İngilizcede iki ayrı kelime var: if ve unless. Unless'in içinde 'değilse' anlamı gizli, o yüzden yanına ayrıca 'not' koymazsın.

reading.title: The fire drill
reading.text:
On Wednesday morning, the fire alarm rings at Lincoln Elementary. It is only a drill, but nobody knows the exact time. That is the point of a drill: if people prepare, they stay safe in a real emergency.

Hafsa is helping in Ms. Carter's class today. Before school, Ms. Carter tells her the plan. "If the alarm rings, we stop what we are doing. We leave the room in a line, and the last student closes the door. Unless the hallway is full of smoke, we use the main exit."

Now the alarm is loud and the plan is real. Hafsa says, "Please stand up and walk calmly. Don't run, and don't take your backpacks." The children line up quickly. Hafsa carries the attendance list, because the teacher counts the students outside. In the hallway, other classes are walking too. Nobody hurries or shouts.

On the playground, every class gathers in its own place. Hafsa counts twenty-two students. Twenty-two! Nobody is missing. She gives the number to Mr. Brown, who writes it on his clipboard. After five minutes, the principal says, "Good job, everyone. You may go back inside."

On the way back, a little girl asks, "If there is a real fire, will we do the same thing?" Hafsa smiles. "Yes. If we practice, we know exactly what to do, and we stay calm."

questions.q: What is happening at the school on Wednesday?
What does the last student do when the class leaves?
options: He or she turns on the lights.
He or she closes the door.
He or she counts the students.
questions.whyTr: Metin: 'the last student closes the door.'

questions.q: What should the students NOT take outside?
Why does Hafsa carry the attendance list?
options: The teacher counts the students outside with it.
The principal wants to read it.
It tells the time of the drill.
questions.whyTr: Metin: 'the teacher counts the students outside.'

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Hafsa, before you start, let me explain the emergency plan.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Yes, please. I'm a little worried.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Don't worry. If you hear a long alarm, it's a fire drill. Take your students outside.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Unless the hallway is blocked, use the blue exit near the gym. If it's blocked, use the back door.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: And what if the alarm is a different sound?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Three short alarms mean lockdown. If you hear three short alarms, lock the door and turn off the lights.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Do the students stay in the classroom?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Yes. They sit quietly on the floor. Unless you get a message from the office, nobody leaves the room.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Keep it with you, but use it only for emergencies.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you. I feel much more prepared now.

questions.q: What does a long alarm mean?
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: 'If you hear a long alarm, it's a fire drill.'

options: The blue exit near the gym
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: 'Unless the hallway is blocked, use the blue exit near the gym.'

questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: 'Three short alarms mean lockdown.'

questions.q: What do students do during a lockdown?
options: They sit quietly on the floor.
questions.whyTr: Mr. Brown: 'They sit quietly on the floor.'

writing.promptTr: Öğrencilere yangın tatbikatı için kısa bir güvenlik notu yaz. En az üç if cümlesi ve bir unless cümlesi kullan.
writing.promptEn: Write a short safety note to students about a fire drill. Use at least three if-sentences and one unless-sentence.
frames: Unless your teacher says something different, ...
writing.model: Dear students, please read our fire drill rules. If you hear the alarm, stop what you are doing. Leave your backpack at your desk, and walk to the door in a line. Don't run, and don't talk. Unless your teacher says something different, use the main exit. If the hallway is full of smoke, use the back door. When you are outside, stay with your class. Your teacher counts everyone. Nobody goes back inside unless the principal says it is safe. If you don't understand a rule, ask your teacher. Practice makes us safe. Thank you, Hafsa
checklistTr: If cümlelerinde present simple, sonuçta talimat veya present simple var mı?
'Unless' cümlesinde olumlu fiil kullandın mı (unless you don't değil)?
